# 14 Render author styles, links and click hooks, and wire onClick

## Outcome

Author styling reaches the SVG as inline `style` attributes, a class with an allowed `href` is
wrapped in a link, a class with a callback carries a click hook, and `render()` gains an optional
`onClick` handler that receives those clicks. This ticket also records the ADR for how author
styling coexists with the token-based theme.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A class with resolved style declarations renders them in that element's `style` attribute,
  in declaration order; a class with none renders no `style` attribute.
- [ ] A class with an allowed `href` is wrapped in `<a class="siren-link" href="...">`; a tooltip
  renders as a `<title>` inside the class group.
- [ ] A class with a callback carries `data-siren-click` naming the callback and any literal
  argument, and is **not** wrapped in an `<a>`.
- [ ] Layout carries the model's resolved styles and interactions onto `PositionedClass`. A class
  named by two interactions resolves **last-wins**, matching the policy ticket 13 already set for
  a later `style` statement on the same class — decide nothing new, just apply it consistently and
  test it.
- [ ] `render(source, container, { onClick })` invokes the handler with the class id and the
  callback target when such an element is clicked; clicking a class with no interaction invokes
  nothing.
- [ ] `render()` without `onClick` renders the same SVG and clicking throws nothing.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0008-author-styling-sits-alongside-the-token-theme.md` records the decision: the
  `--siren-*` token theme stays the global default for every diagram (ADR-0004 unchanged), author
  directives are a local per-document override emitted as inline styles, and the rejected
  alternative was generating an in-SVG `<style>` block with generated class names. Follow the
  existing ADR format.


- [ ] Any `siren-*` class you newly emit has a matching rule in `theme/default.css`. The coverage
  test in `theme/default.test.ts` (added by ticket 16, which now runs before this one) fails
  otherwise — that guard exists precisely so a new class cannot ship unthemed, which is how the
  sequence board shipped an invisible diagram.

## Test seam

`renderClassDiagramToSVG(diagram): SVGSVGElement` (component, jsdom) for the markup, and
`render(source, container, { onClick })` (integration, jsdom, dispatching a real click event) for
the handler.

  empirically before the scope was widened.)
